method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: How Nvidia turmoil and a Democratic Congress could reshape the AI trade, according to ETF experts
Equities.summary: ETF experts say Nvidia’s leadership turmoil and Democratic control of Congress could shift AI demand to the benefit of other Big Tech stocks, rival chipmakers.
Equities.reason: Directly addresses leadership shock at the center of the AI trade — increases uncertainty for Nvidia and the AI-led rally, reinforcing a negative equity narrative for tech and concentrated growth names.

Equities.title: Stocks Slide as Tech Selloff Worsens, Oil Rebounds: Markets Wrap
Equities.reason: Broad market wrap showing worsening tech-led selloff — signals a market regime shift away from narrow AI leadership and higher systemic risk for equities.

Equities.title: Stock futures slip as traders brace for Nvidia earnings, Anthropic IPO this week
Equities.reason: Event-driven risk: concentrated focus on Nvidia earnings and a major AI IPO raises near-term volatility and downside risk for futures and the broader market.

Equities.title: AI selloff resumes as Nvidia earnings loom
Equities.reason: Reuters confirms resumption of the AI-driven selloff tied to Nvidia event risk — reinforces negative momentum in growth/AI equities and flow instability.

Equities.title: Anthropic’s IPO lands as the embattled AI trade looks for a much-needed bright spot
Equities.summary: Anthropic's IPO has outsized importance in the tech industry, which is heavily invested in the AI lab and is desperate for some positive momentum.
Equities.reason: Potential stabilizer for the AI sector if the IPO succeeds; treated as a lower-relevance counterpoint to the prevailing negative momentum.

Equities.title: Jensen Huang discusses comeback as Nvidia CEO with allies
Equities.summary: Tech supporters lobby chipmaker’s board to reinstate former head after he resigned following affair with alleged Chinese spy
Equities.reason: Governance/de-risking signal: a potential return of the former CEO would likely calm some investor concerns and reduce downside risk for Nvidia and the AI complex.

Equities.title: China’s economic activity slows more than expected in October
Equities.summary: Beijing has pushed to speed up budget spending to overcome weaker growth
Equities.reason: Weaker China activity is a material macro drag on global cyclical demand and EM-linked equities, adding to the negative backdrop for global markets already hit by tech volatility.

Equities.title: Asian shares fall before Nvidia earnings, Anthropic IPO test tech rally
Equities.reason: Regional spillover: Asian equities are pricing in Nvidia event risk, showing cross-border contagion from US tech to global equity sentiment.

Equities.title: The Month That Rocked the AI Trade and Rewired Wall Street
Equities.reason: Framing piece on structural change in market positioning away from concentrated AI leadership — supports the dominant narrative of a broader repricing of tech exposure.

Rates.title: Fed’s Schmid: Inflation running too hot, central bank has some work to do
Rates.summary: Kansas City Federal Reserve (Fed) President Jeffrey Schmid said on Sunday that inflation is running too hot, and the central bank has some work to do on inflation.
Rates.reason: High-profile Fed official stressing persistent inflation increases odds of further tightening/higher-for-longer policy — clear negative for bond prices (yields up). Rated highly relevant given Fed signaling to markets.

Rates.title: BoE’s Pill: Further rate rises needed to combat inflation
Rates.summary: Bank of England (BoE) Chief Economist Huw Pill said over the weekend that additional rate hikes are needed to combat inflation. Pill added that he expects further rises to be necessary in 2027, over and above the increase at the next meeting on December 17.
Rates.reason: Senior BoE official explicitly calling for more hikes raises gilt/yield pressure — negative for bond prices. Strong relevance due to direct policy guidance for the UK.

Rates.title: Fed’s Collins: Steady gradual path for rate hikes appropriate amid risks on both sides
Rates.summary: Boston Federal Reserve (Fed) President Susan Collins said on Saturday that she supported a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better managed economic uncertainties.
Rates.reason: Fed official endorses continued rate increases but at a gradual pace — negative for bonds (yields up) but less aggressive than hawkish comments; medium relevance.

Rates.title: BoJ’s Takata calls for nimble, data-dependent rate hikes rather than a fixed pace
Rates.summary: Bank of Japan (BoJ) board member Hajime Takata said on Monday that the central bank should not carry out rate hikes at a fixed pace and size, but instead needs to take nimble and data-dependent actions in response to the price and economic environment in Japan
Rates.reason: BoJ official signalling readiness for discretionary rate hikes suggests upward pressure on JGB yields; relevant for global rates given BoJ's long-standing impact on global bond positioning.

Rates.title: Bond Drought in Emerging Markets Lifts Prices as Sales Slump 41%
Rates.reason: EM issuance slump is tightening supply and lifting bond prices (yields down) — a material countervailing force to global hawkish narrative; meaningful relevance for EM rates and cross-market flows.

Rates.title: Roughed-Up Bond Traders Look to Fedspeak, Minutes for Next Move
Rates.reason: Market piece noting bond traders are jittery and focused on Fed communications — implies continued sensitivity to hawkish messaging and potential for further yield volatility (negative for bond prices).

Rates.title: Japan’s economy contracts for the first time in a year
Rates.summary: Weak consumer spending and record-breaking rains damp GDP growth and complicate interest rate plans
Rates.reason: Japanese GDP contraction eases near-term pressure on BoJ to tighten, which can weigh on yields less or push them down — positive for bond prices in Japan and a modest global dampener to tightening expectations.

Rates.reason: FX piece explicitly tying currency moves to rising Fed hike bets — indirectly signals higher US yield expectations. Included with modest relevance because FX focus provides transmission into rates expectations.

Rates.title: Indonesian Rupiah struggles as US Dollar gains on hawkish Fed odds
Rates.summary: USD/IDR gains ground after posting modest losses in the previous day, trading around 18,280 during Asian hours on Monday. The pair is moving higher as the US Dollar (USD) draws strength from growing speculation that the US central bank will raise interest rate
Rates.reason: FX move linked to rising Fed hike speculation — signals greater US rate expectations and potential pressure on EM bond markets; included with limited relevance (FX-led transmission rather than primary rates release).

Rates.title: Economic calendar: Markets await Monday speech by Fed chair Kevin Warsh
Rates.reason: Anticipation of a Fed chair speech increases near-term rate volatility risk; modestly negative for bonds given current hawkish backdrop but mainly signal/flow risk ahead of the event.

Rates.title: Kazakhstan plans tokenized government bonds in first quarter after $22 million note sale
Rates.reason: Market-structure innovation around sovereign issuance (tokenized bonds) can incrementally improve distribution/liquidity for government debt — small positive for bond markets, low immediate macro relevance.

FX.title: United States Dollar Index holds gains above 103.50 on hawkish Fed comments
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 103.45 in the Asian trading hours on Monday.
FX.reason: DXY strength on hawkish Fed comments is a broad USD-positive signal that pressures major USD/FX pairs and underpins a risk-off USD-dominant market impulse; high relevance for FX flows and positioning.

FX.title: Euro softens below 1.1050 as traders ramp up Fed rate hike bets
FX.summary: The EUR/USD pair declines to around 1.1025 during the early Asian trading hours on Monday. Growing speculations that the US central bank will lift the interest rate in the December policy meeting support the US Dollar (USD) against the Euro (EUR).
FX.reason: EUR/USD weakness is directly tied to rising Fed hike expectations and USD strength — a core USD-centric driver for FX markets with material impact on majors.

FX.title: Japanese Yen strengthens as intervention warnings offset weaker Japan GDP
FX.summary: The USD/JPY pair edges lower to near 159.80 during the early Asian trading hours on Monday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) despite the weaker-than-expected Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.
FX.reason: JPY appreciation amid intervention warnings is an important FX-specific narrative — signals potential policy/FX intervention that can materially support JPY versus USD despite weaker domestic growth.

FX.title: British Pound declines to near 1.3200 as Fed hike bets rise
FX.summary: The GBP/USD pair softens for a fifth consecutive session near 1.3210 during the early European trading hours on Monday. The US Dollar (USD) edges higher against the British Pound (GBP) as traders ramp up bets on the Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening next year.
FX.reason: GBP weakness is being driven by USD strength via Fed hike repricing; meaningful for G10 FX but secondary to DXY/EUR moves — shows broadening USD bid across majors.

FX.title: Canadian Dollar weakens against US Dollar amid Fed rate hike bets, falling oil prices

FX.title: Australian Dollar declines below 0.6800 on hawkish Fed, Chinese data in focus
FX.summary: The AUD/USD pair declines to near 0.6775 during the early Asian session on Monday. The US dollar (USD) edges higher against the Australian Dollar (AUD) on hawkish comments from Federal Reserve (Fed) officials.
FX.reason: AUD weakness is driven by USD strength and softer China data — combines Fed-driven USD flows with demand-side China exposure important for risk-sensitive FX.

FX.reason: Bank commentary pointing to further EUR downside toward 1.1000 reinforces the prevailing USD-strength narrative; analyst view useful for tactical EUR/USD risk but less than macro DXY signals.

FX.summary: The Japanese economy arrived at 0% over the quarter in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026, the preliminary report published by the Cabinet Office showed on Monday. This reading followed a 0.4% growth recorded in Q2 and missed market expectations of a 0.1% expansio

FX.title: Yen steady against euro and dollar after soft Japanese GDP data
FX.reason: Newswire confirmation that yen remained steady despite soft GDP underscores the dominance of FX intervention/backstop narrative over pure macro data in JPY moves — modest positive for JPY.

FX.title: New Zealand Dollar holds near April 2025 low after China's data as USD strength persists
FX.summary: The NZD/USD pair enters a bearish consolidation phase after touching its lowest level since April 2025 during the Asian session on Monday, reacting little to China's macro data dump.
FX.reason: NZD near multi-month lows tied to persistent USD strength and weaker China data — relevant for EM/commodity-linked FX but smaller-than-major-USD moves.

FX.title: Indian Rupee rises on foreign, corporate inflows, lower oil prices
FX.summary: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains ground against the US Dollar (USD) during Monday's Asian trading hours, rebounding from two consecutive days of losses.
FX.reason: INR strength driven by portfolio and corporate inflows is a localized EM FX positive; limited spillover to G10 but relevant for EM FX flows and India positioning.

FX.title: UK, Singapore, and Thailand central banks test cross-border FX settlement as stablecoins gain ground
FX.reason: Central bank trials of cross-border FX settlement using stablecoins are an FX-infrastructure theme that could gradually alter settlement frictions and cross-border FX flows; structural, low immediate market impact.

FX.title: The Bank of England, the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and the Bank of Thailand: Project Meridian FX APAC
FX.reason: Official Project Meridian release confirms cross-border FX settlement experimentation at the central-bank level — reinforces structural adoption narrative and complements other settlement/stablecoin reports.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD hits yearly lows below $47.50 amid hawkish Fed sentiment
Commodities.summary: Silver price (XAG/USD) extends its losses for the third successive day, trading around $47.50 per troy ounce during Asian hours on Monday. Silver prices fell to a yearly low of $47.34, pressured by a strengthening US Dollar (USD) and elevated Treasury yields.
Commodities.reason: Silver at yearly lows; explicit link to stronger USD and higher Treasury yields. Dominant tone = bearish for precious metals driven by hawkish Fed / USD strength, moderate-high relevance for the silver market.

Commodities.title: Gold weakens below $3,850, fresh low since October 2025 amid Fed hike bets, bullish USD
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) weakens further below $3,850 during Monday’s early European session, hitting a fresh low since early October 2025 amid a bearish fundamental backdrop.
Commodities.reason: Gold hitting fresh lows with direct attribution to Fed rate-hike bets and USD strength. Strong directional signal for bearish precious-metals pressure; high relevance for gold market sentiment.

Commodities.title: Gold edges higher as investors await Warsh remarks for rate signals
Commodities.reason: Short-term uptick tied to expectations around a Fed-speech (Warsh). Minor, transient bullish signal that is lower relevance versus prevailing Fed/USD-driven bearish backdrop.

Commodities.summary: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around $87.00 per barrel during Asian hours on Monday.
Commodities.reason: Price decline with explicit narrative that a Middle East supply surplus is outweighing regional attacks. Net bearish for oil; moderate relevance as it reflects prevailing flows and risk premium compression.

Commodities.title: WTI Price Forecast: Bears seem hesitant above $87.00; 200-EMA/50% Fibo. holds the key

Commodities.reason: Technical/price-forecast piece (lower relevance by framework). Slight bearish bias near $87 with limited follow-through—keeps relevance capped.

Commodities.reason: EIA forecast of notable Alaskan production growth increases physical supply expectations. Net bearish for crude prices; fairly high relevance given official EIA supply projection.

Commodities.title: U.S. crude oil imports from Venezuela in July were highest since 2017
Commodities.summary: In July 2026, U.S. imports of crude oil from Venezuela averaged 701,000 barrels per day (b/d), the most since May 2017, before decreasing to 655,000 b/d in August, according to data published in our Petroleum Supply Monthly
Commodities.reason: Higher Venezuelan crude flows to the U.S. add to near-term supply/demand balance; bearish for U.S. crude pricing with a clear supply-transmission—moderate relevance.

Commodities.title: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
Commodities.summary: As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructur
Commodities.reason: Potential Gulf Coast production shut-ins represent a tangible supply disruption risk for crude. Bullish near-term price implication; moderate-high relevance due to physical supply impact.

Commodities.title: China’s Teapot Refiners Turn to Trading Giants as Iran Oil Ebbs
Commodities.reason: Reports that Iranian oil flows to China are ebbing and that refineries are shifting sourcing indicate tighter regional supply; modestly bullish for oil given China's significance for demand and flows.

Commodities.title: Japan's economy unexpectedly contracts in third-quarter as elevated energy costs bite
Commodities.summary: Energy subsidies for households had reportedly expired in September, exposing the economy to the higher energy prices brought about by the Iran war.
Commodities.reason: An economic contraction tied to elevated energy costs points to weaker demand growth in a major economy; slightly bearish for commodity demand, but lower direct relevance versus supply/price pieces.

Crypto.reason: Broad, market-wide narrative: persistent selloff, dwindling risk appetite and flow-driven weakness across major crypto assets. High relevance because it summarizes the dominant market regime and trader sentiment, amplifying downside pressure.
